central.text: Time-of-use or heat-pump electricity tariffs make heat pumps cheaper to run

supporting.by: Bernard 2024 (NBER), UK heat pumps and a time-of-use tariff

central.text: Payback for a heat pump varies widely with climate, fuel prices and the equipment it replaces

central.text: Heat pump efficiency and capacity fall as the outdoor temperature drops

supporting.by: CEE 2017, cold-climate heat pumps in Minnesota
supporting.note: Measured heat-pump-only cycles averaged COP about 1.3 at the 10F change point rising to 3.0-4.5 at 50-60F; outdoor temperature had the largest effect on COP across six Minnesota sites.
supporting.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

supporting.by: Wilson 2024 (NREL and LBNL), heat pumps for all?
supporting.note: Capacity retention curves from lab and NEEP manufacturer data fall from 100% of rated output at 47F to 47% (single-speed) or 85% (cold-climate) at 5F.
supporting.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

supporting.by: Deetjen 2021, private economics of US residential heat pumps
supporting.note: Heat pump efficiency falls with ambient temperature, and at low temperatures the load can exceed capacity so the model falls back to resistance heat (COP 1).
supporting.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

supporting.by: Cadmus 2016, ductless mini-split evaluation (MA and RI)
supporting.note: The evaluation states unit efficiency drops as outdoor temperature drops and estimates from manufacturer data that capacity falls about 20% from 17 F to 5 F at fixed airflow; about half the units could not meet the space heating load below 17 F.
supporting.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

supporting.by: PNNL 2025, DOE Cold Climate Heat Pump Challenge field results
supporting.note: Heating COPs rose steadily with outdoor temperature (median 1.6 in the cold bins up to about 5.2), and the report notes conventional heat pumps lose capacity below 40 F and keep only a fraction in the teens.
supporting.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

supporting.by: RMI 2018, the economics of electrifying buildings
supporting.note: The cold-climate Mitsubishi unit RMI models has a COP at max capacity that falls from 3.5 at 47F to 2.1 at 17F and 1.4 at -13F; the report shows efficiency falling but gives no capacity figures.
supporting.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

supporting.by: CEE 2018, ducted and ductless cold-climate heat pumps in the field
supporting.note: A 1-ton ductless unit in northern Minnesota held its median capacity from 10F to -15F but delivered only about 2,600 Btu/h (about 20% of its rated 5F capacity) between -20F and -25F.
supporting.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

supporting.by: Edwards 2024, inequities in heat pump bill savings
supporting.note: Edwards fits heat pump COP from the NEEP database as a linear function of outdoor temperature (COP = 0.05T + 1.6 above 5F), with single-stage units dropping to about COP 1 below 5F; the source covers efficiency only, not capacity.
supporting.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

supporting.note: Older heat pumps lose efficiency in colder temperatures, less so for newer models; the passage says nothing about capacity.

supporting.by: RMI 2018, the economics of electrifying buildings
supporting.note: RMI notes that ground-source heat pumps use less energy on the coldest days because ground temperature stays moderate, but have historically cost significantly more than air-source because of drilling.
supporting.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

supporting.by: Wilson 2024 (NREL and LBNL), heat pumps for all?
supporting.note: Ground-source heat pumps offer greater efficiency and cold-climate performance than air-source but are an even more expensive solution; stated, not analysed.
supporting.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

qualifying.by: Less 2021 (LBNL), cost of decarbonization retrofits
qualifying.note: LBNL: ground-source heat pumps were the most expensive type, at nearly three times the total system cost of ductless and ducted air-source systems; the report does not test the 'run cheaper' half of the claim.
qualifying.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

qualifying.by: Canadian Climate Institute 2023, heat pumps pay off
qualifying.note: Ground-source heat pumps are highly efficient but more complex and expensive to install because of drilling; running costs are not quantified and they are left out of the model.
qualifying.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded
